subject: Finly discovery recap — latency & concurrency targets
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Samir Gupta <samir@finly.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-15T15:02:00Z
Subject: Finly discovery recap — latency & concurrency targets

Samir — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned.

High-level pain points you shared:
- User-facing responses are showing high tail latency (p95 spikes) during peak usage windows.
- Streaming UX feels sluggish: initial token and early partials are delayed, hurting the real-time experience.
- Current infra is expensive to scale and lacks predictable SLOs; bursts cause degraded latency.

Current stack (as discussed):
- In-house transformer inference on GCP (custom serving stack)
- Model: in-house finetuned Llama variant (~13B) running FP16 on A2s
- Autoscaling based on CPU/GPU utilization; no prefix/KV cache in production

Success criteria you gave us:
- P95 user-facing latency <= 200ms (target) — absolute must for the new feature
- Initial streaming token latency < 120ms; ideally < 100ms for a snappy UX
- Sustained concurrency: ~150 qps baseline, bursts up to ~350 qps during events
- Zero visible errors/retries during peak (95%+ successful responses)

Key risks/constraints:
- Must not materially regress output quality vs current model (Finly will validate with eval prompts)
- PCI/PHI data: logs and samples need to be handled per your security process (we discussed redaction)

Proposed next steps:
1) You share anonymized latency traces / p95 profile and a 24h traffic sample (we can accept CSV exported from your monitoring) — I’ve attached a sample CSV schema request.
2) Technical deep-dive with Aditya (SE) to map model footprint and exact request shapes — propose Monday 11/18 10am PT.
3) POC plan: Redwood Dedicated POC (2-GPU baseline) with KV warming + streaming enabled; we’ll measure p50/p95 and initial token times.
4) Redwood to provide an estimated cost and configuration options (Hosted, Dedicated, Private) after the deep-dive.

Attachments: finly_p95_latency_profile.csv (schema)

If this captures everything, I’ll schedule the deep-dive and share an action tracker.

Thanks,
—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0142

From: Samir Gupta <samir@finly.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-16T10:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Finly discovery recap — latency & concurrency targets

Thanks Marissa — this is great and accurate. A few clarifications from our side: 

- The p95 target we mentioned is specifically for user-facing interactive requests (not for nightly batch jobs). Our observed p95 during peak is ~850–920ms, which is what’s causing user complaints.
- Streaming: our current initial token latency is ~250ms on average — that’s what feels slow. We want initial token under 120ms, ideally <100ms, and early partials within ~80–100ms to feel real-time.
- Concurrency: baseline sustained ~150 qps (weekday business hours), but we see spikes to 300–350 qps for up to 10–15 minutes during product events.

Security and compliance: we can share redacted logs; will need an NDA for any raw samples with PII/PHI.

Decision timeline: we’re aiming to select a vendor and start a POC within 3–4 weeks — budget sign-off expected by Dec 10.

I’ve attached an early SLA draft for your review (SLA-draft.pdf). We can discuss Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs in the deep-dive — cost predictability is important for us.

Appreciate the quick follow-up. Monday 11/18 10am PT works for us for the deep-dive.

—
Samir Gupta
VP Product, Finly
samir@finly.com | +1 (650) 555-1822
Attachments: SLA-draft.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Samir Gupta <samir@finly.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-17T09:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Finly discovery recap — latency & concurrency targets

Samir — perfect, thanks for the clarifications and the SLA draft. Confirming: deep-dive scheduled for Monday 11/18 10am PT (I’ll send the calendar invite).

What we’ll prepare before the call:
- Aditya will run through likely optimizations (quantization, KV caching strategy, batching strategy, and kernel/hw mapping).
- Preliminary Dedicated configuration options and back-of-envelope cost for the POC.
- A short checklist for the logs/sample we need from Finly (redaction guidance included).

POC outline (high level):
1) Shared redacted logs + traffic sample -> Redwood baseline analysis
2) POC on Dedicated (2x GPU) with KV warming & streaming enabled for a 48–72h test window
3) Measure p50/p95, initial token latency, and error rates at baseline and burst traffic profiles
4) Iterate: tune batching/quantization, then re-run measurements

If you can share the redacted traces and a 24h representative traffic sample before the deep-dive (or within 48h after), we can get started quickly.

Thanks — looking forward to the tech session.

—
Marissa

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T09:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Finly discovery recap — latency & concurrency targets

Marissa — looping in a quick technical checklist ahead of the session. I’ll own the deep-dive.

What I need from Finly (minimal):
- Model artifact details (approx parameter count, tokenizer, sequence length used in prod)
- A redacted 24h request log with timestamps, prompt lengths, and response sizes (CSV preferred)
- Peak concurrency windows (time ranges) and any synthetic load profiles you’ve used

What we’ll test for the POC:
- Quantization (4-bit / 8-bit) impact on both latency and generation quality
- KV cache warming and prefix caching to reduce p95 for repeated prefixes
- Continuous batching settings to balance throughput vs tail latency at 150–350 qps
- Streaming partials: measure initial token latency and inter-token latency; enable low-latency kernels for streaming where possible

Preliminary recommendation: likely start with a Dedicated baseline (2x high-memory GPUs) with aggressive KV warming for the POC. If we see model compatibility issues, fallback to a mixed-hosted approach for critical routes.

I’ll prepare a short slide with expected tuning levers and a test plan for Monday.

—
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.com
